Subject: Post-call: pricing sensitivity scenarios & next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for taking time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our discovery: 

Recap (what we heard)
- Primary use case: real-time summarization + semantic search for analyst workflows (multi-turn, average prompt ~120 tokens; responses ~280 tokens).
- Expected pilot volume: 5M–20M user-generated tokens/month in month 1, scaling to ~50M/month by Q4 if initial metrics look good.
- Budget band mentioned: $8k–$30k/month for pilot+early production depending on unit economics and SLA.

Key pricing questions we agreed to clarify
1) Target effective price you want to see (you mentioned target $/1M tokens during call) — can you confirm a target range?
2) Will you consider a committed reserved capacity (monthly commit) vs. pay-as-you-go? Reserved reduces unit cost but requires a commit.
3) Procurement lead contact and preferred invoice cadence (monthly vs. quarterly vs. annual prepay).

What Im attaching for review: 
- redwood-pricing-calculator.xlsx: sensitivity scenarios (shared-hosted vs. dedicated-reserved, caching assumptions).
- token-sensitivity.csv: simple CSV you can drop into your internal model (volumes x cache% x unit price).
- draft-invoice-estimate.pdf: example invoice layout and two pricing scenarios.

What I recommend next
- You: confirm a target $/1M tokens range and whether procurement wants to see a committed vs. variable quote (reply to this thread).
- Us: well produce a one-page commercial summary and a 30-day pilot proposal if you prefer reserved capacity trial.
- Schedule: can we lock 30 minutes next week to walk through the attached calc? Im available Tue/Wed 9–12 PT.

Regards,

Alex — great, thanks. Ive attached the scenarios you asked for and pulled a few quick numbers below for the 20M tokens/month case to make the differences explicit. All numbers are illustrative and assume the model family we discussed (open-vic-like baseline) on our hosted tier unless noted.

Scenario A — Hosted (pay-as-you-go)
- Assumptions: raw tokens processed = 20M/month; avg model cost base = $0.75 / 1k tokens before caching
- Caching: 40% effective prefix/KV cache hit rate -> effective billable tokens = 12M/month
- Unit math: $0.75 / 1k -> $750 / 1M tokens gross; after 40% cache effective spend = $9,000/month -> effective $450 / 1M billed tokens seen

Scenario B — Dedicated reserved capacity (3-month trial commit)
- Assumptions: reserved reduces base model execution cost by ~25% and gives dedicated KV cache efficiency -> base cost ~$0.56 / 1k tokens
- Effective caching smaller delta because dedicated pools increase cache hit locality; with 40% cache -> billable 12M tokens -> spend ~$6,720/month -> effective ~$336 / 1M tokens

Observations and notes
- Cache behavior: the largest swings come from cache hit rate — if hit rate is 20% the hosted effective $/1M jumps ~30% vs 40%. I included a tab in the calculator that lets you sweep cache% and monthly volumes.
- Commitment: reserved commitment materially reduces unit cost when volumes are steady. For a 3-month pilot I can model a stepped commit (lower first-month commit) to reduce risk.
- Invoice examples: draft-invoice-estimate.pdf contains two line-items (compute tokens, storage/cache surcharge) and an optional reserved capacity credit line.

Next steps Id propose
1) Confirm youd like the 30-minute walkthrough Tue 10am PT (Im booking tentative now).
2) Procurement: if you can share any contract constraints (PO terms, required SLAs, tax info) well include them in the pilot SOW.
3) Ill share a short one-page summary of the two scenarios for your finance lead.

Hi Alex — quick technical note from the SE side. A couple of things we built into the calculator youll see: 

- Cache modeling: we separate prefix caching (repeated prompts) vs. KV cache (context reuse); prefix caching yields higher effective token savings for retrieval-heavy workflows.
- Latency delta: reserved pools reduce p95 generation latency by ~15–30ms in our tests for the same model size; if your product is latency-sensitive that often justifies the committed trial.
- Implementation ask: to validate the 40% cache scenario wed want a sample workload (anonymized prompt logs) for one week — we can run a quick sim and return a cache projection.

Ill join the Tue 10am PT call and walk the calc. Karthik, Ill draft the one-pager for finance after the walkthrough.

Best,
